correctness.rationale: Real octagon norm N(u,v)=max(|u|,|v|,(|u|+|v|)/sqrt2). Parameter swapping x and y shows J(lambda)=J(1-lambda); for 0<lambda<=1/2 the published general bound J(lambda,X)<=lambda J(X)+|2lambda-1| (Liu et al Theorem 5.2) and independently published classical J(X8)=sqrt2 imply upper T=1-(2-sqrt2)lambda. Set r=sqrt2-1, x=(-r,1), y=(1,r), both norm one. Expand p=lambda x+(1-lambda)y=(1-sqrt2 lambda,r+(2-sqrt2)lambda); q=lambda x-(1-lambda)y=(-T,sqrt2 lambda-r). For half interval p coordinates nonnegative, <=T, diagonal (p1+p2)/sqrt2=T, hence N(p)=T. q1=-T and |q2|<=r T, verified by splitting at lambda=1-1/sqrt2 into affine factors 2(2-sqrt2)lambda and 2(sqrt2-1)(1-2lambda); hence N(q)=T. Endpoint lambda=1/2 agrees J(X8)/2=sqrt2/2. Parameter symmetry gives complete exact J(lambda)=1-(2-sqrt2)min(lambda,1-lambda). The independent local symbolic factorization reproduces every inequality, not a finite grid proof. C depends on the cited universal bound and published classical J(X8); those premises are explicitly identified.
